parsed.why: No criminalisation or trans-specific restrictions; visitor-facing exposures undocumented. Weak hate-crime enforcement with court-ordered reopenings shows functioning but imperfect recourse. Dated incidents, no documented trans targeting; thin-data climate signal mildly positive.

Strong protections (self-ID, GI equality law, marriage equality) and no visitor-facing restrictions; but documented police stops of trans people, 2024 mob attack on two trans people (arrests followed), and birth-sex prison default with on-request transfer partially mitigate.

Criminalisation up to 14 years, enforced against gender-nonconforming people: trans woman sentenced to 8 years, police targeting, violent detentions, forced stripping, state hostility, no recognition or recourse. Organised targeting tier dominates.

No criminalisation or trans-specific laws; documented police assault/torture of LGBT people with no sanction, repeated attacks on LGBT centre, weak hate-crime enforcement, pride violence. Tier-3 societal hostility with thin recourse offsets paper protections.

Currently permissive: hate-crime law, facilities access protected, no visitor-facing restrictions; rollback bills only at first reading, not yet law. Rollback attempt is a climate warning, not a current exposure; the 2006 killing is a dated isolated incident.
